chunks: What was narrated by Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, Ibn Muslim, and al-Halabi, all together, who said: He said:
Do not sit between the two sajdahs like the sitting of a dog.

key_terms.إِقْعَاءِ: the act or manner of sitting known as iq'a
key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: the two sajdahs within a unit of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog; used here as a comparison for the prohibited posture
key_terms.تُقْعِ: sit in the posture of iq'a, a specific seated position

ai.seo_question: What posture is prohibited between the two sajdahs in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling regarding posture in salat (prayer), prohibiting a particular manner of sitting between the two sajdahs. It indicates that the worshipper should avoid an improper or disliked form resembling the sitting posture of a dog.
